item.title: Re: Anomalous Chime Seeking Greenlight.
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for Reply
- Close

I guess my big concern is: what are these testing logs showing? It kinda feels like they might feel…pedestrian; but I think a few showcasing the various melodies it produces could be a fun little middle section.

The logs do showcase are variety of the melodies the chime can produce, though they are often not limited to just songs, but anything that can be considered loosely musical (such as a heart monitor or an all-clear alarm). The intention was to have a recovery log, a testing log, a long term exposure log, and a reverse engineering log. Two of those I've already written in the draft.

Uhhh what children? Are they just a some children who are enamoured by the clock or?

For some reason I didn't want to give away the entire story within the idea critique, but the shop was using foster children, for their small nimble fingers, to manufacturer the SCP. (There is also an implication that it has to be specifically orphaned children for the 'magic' to work).

The test logs feeling awkwardly inserted between the discovery section and the epilogue…

That's my bad for implying the testing logs are between the epilogue and the recovery section. They're not, they're the 2nd to last segment (the last is an audio recording of the chime).

…it might just need some kinda hint as to why the two people responsible made this and what they were intending, y'know?

I wasn't going for any outlandish intentions, the people responsible were using the anomalous nature, and the enamoring factor oft he SCP to sell it for exceptionally large amounts of money.

item.title: Re: Anomalous Chime Seeking Greenlight.
item.content:encoded:
Finally, I can actually critique this.

So, I’m not seeing any major problems. Though I do have a few questions. What does child services have to do with this? This seems more like an SCP that would be more useful for elderly people or someone else who wants to remember something from their life. Usually dealing with children is more about forming new memories than calling back old ones. Also, about the obsession that it places on people. Is it more like a violent obsession, an addiction, or a longing? Because violent obsessions are done to death and personally, I feel a sense of longing for the chimes would go best for the theme you’re trying to set here.

Overall though, I like your SCP. You clearly have thought out what you want it to do and I like the versatility in it’s abilities. From a parent flatlining to the subject themself singing the song the testing logs seem interesting. I’d be interested in reading your draft, if you could PM me the link that’d be great.

item.title: Anomalous Chime Seeking Greenlight.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Genre (Optional): Light-Hearted/Semi-Comedic

Page Layout (Optional): Standard (Modern Header)

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous chime peaks both the local population, and the Foundation's interests, forcing the Foundation to dig into just where this magical melody is coming from.

Central Narrative: A Specialty shop in Southern FL is producing clocks who's chimes enamor their listeners. Towards the end of opening day as the crowd continues to grow and displace traffic, the authorities are alerted, including our very own Foundation. While having to manage crowd control, they find that upstairs of the clock-store is an peculiar workshop where brass fittings, elaborate blueprints, and the Florida Child Services system are coming together to create a lovely anomalous item. Post-haste our illustrious Foundation secures the area and is now able to devote its energy to a favored past-time: testing logs. Including but not limited to logs from the personnel/civilians on the ground, and logs from the Foundation's bunker where testing can be conducted on D-Class in peace. We also have a neat little epilogue with the arrest of the two individuals responsible, and the return of the children to the foster care system.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The chime itself is a melody (3-12 seconds long) that can be heard as any instrument, vocalization, or combination there-of that the listener would agree was the best song/tune they've heard1. This includes, but is not limited to: A lullaby sung by the listeners deceased mother, a D-Class re-hearing the sound of their abusive father's heart monitor flat-line, and the listener themselves singing the ending of a song they had been struggling to write.

Additional Notes: While the SCP is safe (in its contained form, the crank/winding piece is removed), any listener will, over an extended period of time, become obsessive with the clock, and may begin to prioritize listening to the chime over basic bodily needs.

Testing logs are a list of personnel and the melodies they heard, with accompanying notes section (ranging from somber to sarcastic).
Draft upon request.

Footnotes
1. Subjects rarely can guess what the melody will be prior to hearing it, but all recognize it afterward.
